column.text: Bitcoin has surged 22.6% in just one week to hit $79,500 following massive short liquidations totaling three billion dollars, yet the underlying technical structure warns of imminent exhaustion with an RSI reading at 80.18 on the daily timeframe and negative MACD histograms signaling a potential pullback before any continuation can occur. While institutional ETF inflows provided a robust floor today by adding $307 million to reserves, this macro strength is increasingly decoupling from crypto-native momentum as stablecoin supply expands to $261 billion, indicating that dry powder is accumulating rather than immediately deploying into upside rallies. The tape remains technically up-trending in a risk-on regime where continuation longs carry the tailwind of fresh capital entering via record weekly inflows tripling volume since October, but traders must recognize that dollar liquidity is contracting against these assets pushing into significant macro headwinds. This divergence between institutional buying and bearish settlement data creates a fragile environment where failed rallies offer better odds than chasing extended strength without a real catalyst beyond the recent liquidation cascade. The market currently sits in greed territory at 66, driven by headlines of NVIDIA raising AI server prices due to soaring memory costs and Solana cutting mainnet slot times toward its two hundred millisecond goal, but these fundamental upgrades cannot instantly resolve the overbought conditions visible on higher timeframes.
